title: Problem 1
statement_text: Can 3-colouring be solved on diameter-2 graphs in quasi-polynomial time?
context_text: 3-colouring is the decision problem asking whether the input graph $G$ (on $n$ vertices) has a proper colouring with 3 colours; the diameter of a connected graph is the maximum distance between two vertices. A quasi-polynomial-time algorithm runs in time $2^{(\log n)^{O(1)}}$. Restricting the diameter does not give a hereditary class, which makes the usual branching approaches harder. Adding a universal vertex shows that $k$-colouring is NP-hard on diameter-2 graphs for every $k\ge4$ (and, under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, not solvable in time $2^{o(n)}$), and under ETH 3-colouring diameter-4 graphs cannot be done in time $2^{o(n)}$; this leaves 3-colouring on diameter-2 and diameter-3 graphs as the two notorious open cases identified by Paulusma. For diameter 2, Mertzios and Spirakis gave a subexponential algorithm of running time $2^{O(\sqrt{n\log n})}$ for list-3-colouring, and the authors note that the problem might even be solvable in polynomial time, which they call the most intriguing open problem in the area. The paper itself improves 3-colouring on diameter-3 graphs to time $2^{O(n^{2/3-\varepsilon})}$ for any $\varepsilon<1/33$ (previously $2^{O((n\log n)^{2/3})}$, with an ETH lower bound of $2^{\Omega(\sqrt n)}$), and explicitly highlights the quasi-polynomial question for diameter 2 as an intermediate target.
paper_title: Faster 3-colouring algorithm for graphs of diameter 3
